newsitem.title: USA: Carolina Power says Brunswick restart Mon.
newsitem.headline: Carolina Power says Brunswick restart Mon.

text.p: Carolina Power & Light Co plans to restart its 767 megawatt (MW) Brunswick 1 nuclear power plant later today, the company said Monday.
The unit was shut Thursday ahead of Hurricane Fran, which came ashore at Cape Fear on the North Carolina coast, close to the Brunswick facility at Southport, N.C.
"Brunswick 1 should be starting up today and putting power back on the grid by tomorrow," said company spokesman Mike Hughes.
Hughes said the adjacent Brunswick 2 unit, with a rated production capacity of 754 MW, likely would restart Thursday after unit 1 is up and running.

The company said last week there had been some damage from Fran to an administrative and maintenance building at the Brunswick site, but that the power plant itself had weathered the storm's 120 mph winds without problems.
Hughes said the company still has no estimated restart time for its Harris nuclear power plant, an 880 MW unit at New Hill, N.C.
"They are still trying to resolve some issues...the loss of power to sirens in the area, for example," said Hughes, citing backup safety problems related to the hurricane.
The unit tripped off line late September 3 when a water pump and its backup pump failed.
